prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1235; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision involving the insured vehicle. The claimant reports a knee injury from the impact and is not represented by an attorney at this stage.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted with the claim. They confirm several details of the reported damage, though there are no independent witnesses to the collision itself. The vehicle damage is consistent with the described impact.

Entry 3: Confirmed with the police report and statements from the scene that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the crash. The driver is named on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates coverage.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant again. The account of how the collision happened matched what was given in the first contact. A few old scratches on the vehicle may predate this crash and are being noted separately from the current damage.

Entry 5: Medical records show treatment for the knee followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved. The reported injury fits the kind and force of a crash of this type. No earlier injury to the same body area is known.

Entry 6: File reviewed. The injury, vehicle damage, and claimant account are consistent with one another, and the claim is ready for the next level of review.
